title: ui-neumorphism documentation
lede: The documentation site of a 2020 React component library, laid out as two fitness-app screens on one pale surface.
summary: React component library docs: fitness-app cards, a round step counter, and pressed nav tabs on pale blue-gray.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.

styles.note: Clear. Cards, tiles, a round counter, and nav buttons share the pale blue-gray page and rise from it; the active tab is pressed in.

context: The library describes itself as “a react component library designed on the ‘new skeuomorphism’ UI/UX trend”. Repository created on 11 May 2020, MIT License.
observed: A pale blue-gray page with a raised frame around the whole layout and a large blue “UI-Neumorphism” title.
Two phone-sized cards (“Program”, “Plan list”) hold raised tiles, a large raised circle with a runner icon and “8,690”, and raised list rows with thin blue progress rings.
In each bottom bar the active icon sits in a small pressed square.
One blue accent for icons and links; text is near-black sans-serif (Roboto-like). A plain text list of components runs down the left.
interpretation: A faithful web translation of the Dribbble-era fitness concepts, with state shown as pressed versus raised.
Measured: shadows on 70 % of boxes (median offset 2.8 px, median blur 5 px, none hard), borders on 5 %, median radius 8 px.

images.alt: ui-neumorphism documentation: a pale blue-gray page with two raised phone-sized cards showing fitness tiles, a large raised circle with 8,690 steps, and bottom navigation with a pressed active tab.
